text: That is a strange position; when the collision occurred, did your leg appear twisted or pulled outward immediately? Also, can you bear any weight on the right leg right now?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient was involved in a rear-end collision where she was the restrained driver of the back car. She reports immediate onset of pain in both knees and severe pain over the right groin area following the accident.

speaker: Doctor
text: Can you describe the specific mechanism of injury for the right groin—did your hip feel like it was dislocated or forced into an abnormal position during the crash? Additionally, have you noticed any visible deformity of the right thigh compared to the left?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Severe right groin pain. I also have Pain in both knees, Right leg is slightly shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Right Posterior Hip Dislocation.

The specific positioning of your leg—shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated following the rear-end collision—is the classic presentation of this injury. I will confirm this immediately by requesting images of your right hip joint.

REQUEST IMAGES: Right Hip X-Ray AP and Lateral views.
